transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Fluxion CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Owen (SRE), Leah (Finance)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR / health check focused on surge readiness, cost right-sizing, and procurement artifacts.

[00:00] Sara (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, super tight agenda today — runway stress, cost implications, and next steps for the dedicated pilot.
[00:18] Jordan (Fluxion): thanks sarah, yes we've got COO breathing down my neck on "can the system not melt" during events — last month we saw a 4x burst and latency blew past 2s at p95 on our previous infra.
[00:33] Liam (Redwood): yeah we looked at the telemetry you sent earlier, there were a couple KV cache thrash patterns and also prefix caching wasn't being used which increased token counts. quick question — are you currently on Hosted or Dedicated?
[00:47] Priya (Fluxion): currently hybrid, most traffic hits hosted for dev/low-sensitivity, but production inference for billing happens on a reserved pool we manage; we want Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency but need to understand cost.
[01:02] Maya (Redwood): and procurement said they'd need SOC2 + network diagrams + KMS notes before moving forward.
[01:15] Owen (Fluxion): yep and SRE will need an architecture diagram — how the fallback will behave if Dedicated saturates and we route to hosted regionally. we had a weird failover last time where the app retried at the same rate and made it worse.
[01:35] Liam (Redwood): great, we'll show how smart routing handles fallback — policy based routing with circuit-breaker + gradual backoff, and you can pin model variants so the fallback uses a cheaper quantized variant to keep latency bounded. sometimes the docs call it "quant-variant" but internally it's a model family switch.
[01:58] Jordan (Fluxion): the quantized stuff worries our quality folks — any observed delta on generation quality? we can't accept hallucination increases.
[02:13] Liam (Redwood): totally valid — our Optimize module flags quality regressions against your eval set. we can run a quick head-to-head with Fluxion's evals during the 24h stress run and check for semantic diffs.
[02:30] Priya (Fluxion): good. can we get cost numbers with burst usage? the finance team wants worst-case monthly burn if we hit spikes 4x for 48 hours.
[02:45] Leah (Fluxion): and also committed capacity vs on-demand — which is cheaper for us at scale?
[02:53] Sara (Redwood): committed = lower per-token and reserved GPU price; on-demand allows bursts but is more expensive sustained. our Dedicated pricing model includes burst credits and a configurable burst cap; we'll produce a model of committed+burst vs hosted-only.
[03:14] Owen (Fluxion): from a reliability standpoint, how do you handle KV cache population and cold-start of LLM KV caches across autoscale events? we saw cold cache storms.
[03:29] Liam (Redwood): we do continuous batching + warm pool heuristics; when autoscale spins up a new shard we pre-warm KV for common prefixes where your traffic pattern shows reuse. sometimes that pre-warm misses on very long-tail queries. we'll instrument with a warm-miss metric and share it.
[03:50] Jordan (Fluxion): what about multi-region? compliance wants EU only for certain customers, US for others — can routing be per-customer?
[04:05] Sara (Redwood): yes, routing policies can be set at route/token scope — per-tenant region pinning is supported in Private and Dedicated with VPC configs. Hosted can also do geo-routing but data residency assurances are stronger with Private.
[04:20] Priya (Fluxion): procurement asked about audit logs retention for debugting suspicious outputs — we need 12 months.
[04:32] Maya (Redwood): audit logs available; retention is a configurable addon. we also have redaction tools and PII filters we can enable.
[04:45] Leah (Fluxion): ok good. back to cost, rough ballpark: if we commit to a mid-tier reserved pool what does p95 latency look like on 8k context and QPS 150?
[05:00] Liam (Redwood): with current model families we've profiled, p95 around 280-350ms on A100-like nodes with optimized kernels; will vary by model and sequence length distribution. we'll attach the profile sheet from our model catalog.
[05:20] Jordan (Fluxion): earlier you mentioned fallback to quant variant — what's the worst-case quality delta?
[05:27] Liam (Redwood): usually minor for classification/reranking but for open-generation it depends on prompt engineering; we'll label variants with expected quality delta and run your eval set.
[05:40] Owen (Fluxion): run the stress test with our replay patterns — do you need live traffic or can we anonymize replay?
[05:50] Sara (Redwood): replay is fine, prefer anonymized. send the trace and we'll reproduce the spike in a staging Dedicated pool.
[06:02] Priya (Fluxion): one more technical — what about KV cache eviction policy under memory pressure? we had cases where eviction happened in the middle of a session causing context loss.
[06:18] Liam (Redwood): eviction is LRU with session-awareness; we also support sticky caches for hot sessions. if you have long-running conversations you can pin caches to avoid eviction for a TTL.
[06:30] Jordan (Fluxion): great. can you walk through the 24h test plan?
[06:35] Liam (Redwood): plan: 1) deploy a dedicated staging pool sized to your committed spec; 2) replay traffic with 3x baseline then ramp to 4x bursts at random intervals; 3) run model-mix including quant variants and track p50/p95/p99, KV warm-miss, CPU/GPU utilization, and latency tail. we'll also enable our fallback policy to simulate cross-region failover.
[07:00] Sara (Redwood): expected deliverable is a CSV of traces, a dashboard link, and a short write-up with recommendations. target turnaround: 48–72 hours after we get the replay trace.
[07:14] Owen (Fluxion): can you simulate degraded network on the backplane so we can see behavior during partial network partitions?
[07:22] Liam (Redwood): yes we can inject packet loss and latency in the staging env to emulate partial region issues.
[07:31] Priya (Fluxion): procurement is also sensitive to SLA language — they want clarity on failovers and RTO. is there a standard SLA for Dedicated?
[07:43] Maya (Redwood): Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime and latency targets; specifics vary by commit tier. we'll include the SLA appendix in the security pack.
[07:54] Leah (Fluxion): when might we see a price sheet for committed + burst?
[07:58] Sara (Redwood): i'll send an initial estimate by monday — it will include committed tiers and a modeled worst-case burn assuming 48 hours at 4x.
[08:08] Jordan (Fluxion): are there any roadmap items in the next quarter that might affect latency or autoscale behavior?
[08:16] Liam (Redwood): yes two things: kernel-level attention optimization landing in Sept that reduces small-batch latency, and autoscale heuristics improvements that better pre-warm based on historical prefix distribution. both will help tail latency.
[08:33] Jordan (Fluxion): nice. will those require model changes or are they runtime-level?
[08:38] Liam (Redwood): runtime-level, non-invasive. we'll flag models that could benefit from quantization or different attention kernels.
[08:48] Priya (Fluxion): okay on the pilot scope — we want a 4-week pilot with a small committed baseline and burst plan, run the 24h stress test in week 1, then progressively route 20%/50%/100% over weeks to validate.
[09:05] Sara (Redwood): that sounds reasonable. we'll prepare a pilot plan doc and an A/B rollout schedule for canarying.
[09:12] Leah (Fluxion): finance might prefer a 3-month commit with escape clauses if performance or cost deviates — is that negotiable?
[09:21] Maya (Redwood): enterprise contracts often include performance remediation language. sara and legal can follow up.
[09:30] Jordan (Fluxion): any red flags you see from your side before we commit?
[09:34] Liam (Redwood): nothing blocking — just need the replay traffic and confirmation of model mix. also we'll need an internal contact for the pilot who's empowered for quick decisions.
[09:47] Owen (Fluxion): that'll be me for SRE stuff, Priya for evaluation, and Leah for finance approvals.
[09:55] Sara (Redwood): perfect. quick note on the audit logs: we can provide a sample export and show how to integrate with your SIEM.
[10:05] Priya (Fluxion): sounds good, and please ensure PII redaction can be toggled because some customer interactions include PHI.
[10:14] Maya (Redwood): we have redaction and token masking; we'll include the config options in the pack.
[10:22] Jordan (Fluxion): ok let's recap and next steps.
[10:26] Sara (Redwood): recap — Redwood runs 24h stress test with Fluxion replay, share CSV and dashboard; Redwood sends SOC2 + KMS + network diagram + SLA appendix; Fluxion shares replay trace and confirms budget range; schedule pilot kickoff week of Aug 24.
[10:45] Leah (Fluxion): finance will try to confirm by Aug 20.
[10:49] Sara (Redwood): we'll aim to deliver the test results by Aug 18 and docs by Aug 16.
[10:55] Jordan (Fluxion): thanks all, that was productive.
[11:00] Sara (Redwood): thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pilot plan doc.

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings; speaker attribution is best-effort.
notes: Customer emphasized need for worst-case 48h spike modeling and audit log retention; Redwood to validate quality delta for quant variants using customer evals during stress run. Agreed pilot scope: 4-week committed pilot with progressive traffic ramp. Finance and procurement gating items noted.
private_notes: SE to coordinate with infra team to carve a staging pool that matches customer's GPU mix. Flag: quality team to join if evaluation shows >2% semantic regression on critical prompts.
